title: Mix Up Your Practice
heading: Mix Up Your Practice
coreClaim: The chapter argues that interleaving and variation strengthen learning by forcing the learner to discriminate among similar cases and choose the right response instead of repeating one move in a single block.
distinctMechanism: The mechanism is discrimination under changing conditions: mixed practice teaches selection and transfer rather than only repetition.
requiredAnchors: Blocked practice can create misleading smoothness.
Interleaving helps the learner tell similar problems or responses apart.
Mixed practice helps learning travel into later varied situations.
commonMisreadings: Blocked practice is useless at every stage.
specificApplications: Use mixed review sets rather than only grouped drills.
Vary similar scenarios so the learner must identify the right tool.
Keep enough structure that the learner can still see the pattern.
hardEdgeRequirement: Keep the line between productive mixing and chaotic overload visible.
thresholdQuestion: When does mixed practice sharpen discrimination, and when does it scatter attention too much to help?
